_note: News the rules write about the parties: what rival parties go through and do. Placeholders: {short} the party's short name, {name} its full name, {leader} its leader, and the extras named in each entry. 'title' heads the story, 'text' is its body; a one-line entry is a move in the ticker and on the Parties page.

scandal.title: {short} rocked by scandal
scandal.text: Leaked messages show {leader} arranging state contracts for party donors. {short} is in turmoil and trust in politics has fallen.

infighting.title: Open infighting in {short}
infighting.text: A faction inside {name} is openly attacking {leader}. Party members are taking sides.

rebound.title: {leader} wins back the room
rebound.text: A strong conference speech has united {short} again. Its base is energised.

split.title: {name} splits apart
split.text: After months of infighting, a third of {short}'s MPs have walked out. About {freed} million of its loyal voters are now up for grabs. Whoever stands closest to them will pick them up.

copies_you.title: {short} copies your line on {issue}
copies_you.text: Worried about losing voters to you, {leader} has moved {short} toward {toward}. They will compete for the same voters.

fills_niche.title: {short} takes up {side}
fills_niche.text: Nobody was speaking for {side} voters on {issue}, so {leader} has started to. Expect to hear a lot more about it from them.

begins.title: The campaign begins
begins.text: {weeks} weeks to the election. The parties' convoys are on the road, the posters are going up, and from now on every week counts.
